strengths: The distinction between raw model inputs and interpretable explanatory features exposes an important confounding problem. This is useful to researchers working on causal discovery, explainability, and algorithm auditing.

Using FCI and PAGs, together with the knowledge that predictions cannot cause image content, is a principled application of established causal-discovery theory under the stated assumptions. A new discovery algorithm is unnecessary for this contribution to interest TMLR readers.

The manuscript clearly motivates population-level causal explanation and distinguishes it from explanations of individual predictions. The graphical examples and discussion of background knowledge make the central proposal understandable.

The synthetic example and two annotated-image applications make the workflow concrete. The preprocessing details and acknowledgment of ambiguity, annotation requirements, and feature-selection limitations are helpful.
weaknesses: Necessary: Rework the Shapley counterexample in Section 3.3 and Appendix A. When Z3 is omitted, Appendix A.2 still holds its value fixed inside coalition calculations; it does not derive the observable adjustment functional using only Z2. Moreover, if the intended coalition values are do-interventional expectations, Appendix A.1 should propagate interventions on Z2 or Z3 into their descendant Z1. Define the value function precisely and rederive or remove the comparison. The current calculation does not establish the claimed failure specifically due to omitted confounding.

Necessary: Preserve the distinction between possible and definite causes throughout the results. Section 6.3 pools directed and partially directed edges, while Section 6.4 and Figures 9–10 sometimes describe the resulting features as established causes. Bootstrap stability does not resolve ambiguity within a Markov equivalence class. Also, absence of an adjacent edge does not exclude a mediated causal effect: Figure 10 itself permits Cardiomegaly to affect the prediction through Atelectasis. Report these categories separately and use ancestry or appropriately narrower language when discussing causal irrelevance.

Necessary: Address selection in the X-ray experiment. The 120 controls are selected specifically for having 'no findings,' whereas the 120 cases have pneumonia. Selection therefore depends on disease and finding status, potentially changing the conditional independences used by FCI. This requires justification or explicit modeling, particularly because Section 3 dismisses selection bias as irrelevant. Alternatively, narrow the medical conclusions to exploratory hypotheses under unverified sampling assumptions. Clinical plausibility alone does not validate the inferred causes.

Necessary: Establish the reliability of the conditional-independence tests supporting the empirical graphs. With 26 multilevel bird attributes, conditioning sets up to size four, and only 240 X-rays, sparse contingency tables are a substantial concern for asymptotic chi-square tests. Attribute consolidation and bootstrapping do not by themselves establish calibration. Report the actual samples and splits used for graph learning, assess sparse-cell behavior, and provide suitable testing or sensitivity evidence for the principal orientations.

Necessary: Verify the simulation's causal ground truth for the complete image-to-prediction pipeline. Section 5 infers dependence on only H and V from the final logistic layer, but that layer receives imperfect HydraNet detections. Changes to C or T could affect those detections. Clarify whether FCI receives hard labels or probability scores: the reported nonzero C/T coefficients affect scores, although they can leave thresholded labels invariant for binary detector outputs. Controlled shape interventions or an explicitly constrained simulator would substantiate the claimed graph recovery.

Optional: A comparison using the same semantic annotations would better isolate the contribution of causal discovery from the benefit of interpretable features. The present LIME/SHAP examples mainly illustrate differences in representation and explanation scope. Exact executable configurations and larger labels in Figure 8 would also improve usability.
